name: Isolated Arhinencephaly
aliases: Isolated absence of the olfactory bulbs and tracts

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Isolated Arhinencephaly

criteria.description: Complete absence of olfactory bulbs and tracts on neuroimaging
No associated cerebral malformations or midline defects
Confirmed anosmia or severe hyposmia on clinical testing
Exclusion of syndromic causes such as Kallmann syndrome or holoprosencephaly

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of complete absence of olfactory bulbs and tracts on imaging, clinical anosmia, and absence of other cerebral malformations
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires detailed neuroimaging and olfactory function testing to exclude syndromic forms.

typical cognitive abilities

usual head and face structure

normal endocrine function despite smell loss
slight delay in learning skills

slow developmental milestones

head pain related to smell issues

laboratory: Normal endocrine hormone levels excluding hypogonadotropic hypogonadism
imaging: MRI demonstrating complete absence of olfactory bulbs and tracts
Normal cerebral hemispheres without midline defects
genetic: No consistent genetic mutations identified; exclusion of KAL1 and FGFR1 mutations
other: Clinical olfactory testing confirming anosmia or severe hyposmia

distinguishingFeatures: Genetic mutations in KAL1 or FGFR1
Additional midline defects and delayed puberty
Midline cerebral malformations visible on imaging
Facial anomalies such as cyclopia or cleft lip/palate

redFlags: Presence of midline facial anomalies suggesting syndromic diagnosis
Endocrine abnormalities such as delayed puberty or hypogonadism
Neurological deficits beyond anosmia indicating broader brain malformations
references: Neuroimaging in congenital anosmia: absence of olfactory bulbs and tracts, Radiology Journal 2022
Genetic and clinical features of isolated arhinencephaly, Journal of Medical Genetics 2021
